class.name: EngineReactionData
class.brief_description: Optional engine-block torque reaction and torque-driven chassis vibration.
class.description: Assign to [member VehicleConfig.engine_reaction_data]. Settings are copied at setup or [method Vehicle.restart]. Torque acts along the normalized chassis-local [member Vehicle.engine_axis]; reverse the vector for the opposite crankshaft spin direction. A missing resource, disabled resource, or zero axis disables the effect. Reaction opposes engine-generated torque minus engine braking and rotational drag, sampled before clutch coupling. Vibration amplitude scales with actual positive generated torque, including idle feedforward and idle-controller support. Stable idle therefore vibrates even though net engine torque is zero. Limiter cuts and effective throttle (including TCS and turbo) affect the generated torque source. Both reaction and vibration fade with absolute vehicle speed using a smoothstep transition. By default full strength is retained through 5 km/h and no engine chassis torque remains at or above 30 km/h, in forward or reverse. Frequency still follows RPM and phase keeps advancing while faded, avoiding phase jumps when slowing down. This speed fade prevents this effect from adding chassis torque during travel; it does not undo angular motion already present. Vibration is an authored low-frequency sine, not a cylinder firing simulation. Frequency interpolates from idle to redline and is limited to one fifth of the chassis physics tick rate. Substeps accumulate angular impulse and one average world-space torque is applied each physics tick. The sine is integrated analytically per substep and its amplitude is reduced to fit symmetric headroom under the torque cap, preserving its zero mean at constant load. This models engine-block reaction, not complete gearbox/differential housing reaction or elastic engine mounts.

members.member: Enables reaction and vibration after setup/restart.
Nonnegative multiplier of signed engine self torque. Zero disables reaction while retaining vibration.
Nonnegative multiplier of actual generated engine torque, including idle support, before speed fading. Zero disables vibration. No fixed idle amplitude is added.

Maximum engine RPM considered idle for the vibration multiplier, inclusive. Applies at idle and during recovery below idle RPM. Above this threshold the normal vibration strength is used. Copied at setup/restart.

Additional nonnegative vibration amplitude multiplier at or below idle_vibration_max_rpm. Default gives 50% stronger idle vibration. One disables the extra boost; zero suppresses vibration in this RPM range. Steady reaction and frequency are unaffected. Speed fade and torque cap still apply. Copied at setup/restart.
Rumble frequency in Hz at or below idle RPM. Nonnegative; capped at runtime to one fifth of the chassis tick rate. Zero frequency suppresses vibration and pauses phase advancement.
Rumble frequency in Hz at or above redline RPM, interpolated by RPM from idle. Nonnegative; capped at runtime to one fifth of the chassis tick rate.
Nonnegative total torque limit in Nm. Reaction has priority; vibration uses remaining symmetric headroom. Zero suppresses all applied torque.
Nonnegative speed in km/h up to which full reaction and vibration strength is retained. Absolute vehicle speed is used, including reverse travel. Copied at setup/restart.

Speed in km/h at which reaction and vibration reach zero. Smoothly interpolated from speed_fade_start_kph. Runtime fade width is at least 1 km/h, so end values at or below start produce a 1 km/h transition above start. Copied at setup/restart.
